title: Matrix multiplication
instructorPromptText: Write a C program that reads the dimensions and elements of two matrices, verifies if multiplication is possible, computes the product matrix using nested loops, and prints the result.

specGateDimensions.description: Does the program verify that matrix multiplication is mathematically possible (the columns of Matrix A equal the rows of Matrix B) before computing?
specGateDimensions.rationale: Verifies that students write safety validation logic before proceeding with complex mathematical algorithms.

specGateDimensions.description: Does the program implement a triple-nested loop structure correctly to accumulate the sum of products?
specGateDimensions.rationale: Matrix multiplication requires three loops (rows of A, columns of B, and common dimension). Tracking three indices (i, j, k) tests control flow mastery.

specGateDimensions.description: Is the accumulator variable or the target matrix cell initialized to zero before running the dot product summation loop?
specGateDimensions.rationale: Forgetting to initialize variables to 0 before accumulating sums is a classic C error due to garbage values in memory.

expectedDivergences.pattern: Student forgets to initialize the product cell `C[i][j]` to zero before starting the summation loop.
Student uses incorrect bounds or indexes in the innermost loop (e.g. using row size instead of common dimension size).
Student does not check if matrix dimensions are compatible, resulting in undefined behavior or heap buffer reading errors.
Student allocates matrices dynamically using `malloc` rather than using static-size array buffers.
Student prints the output in a single line or raw sequence instead of a formatted grid structure.
